children.text: Oscillator damped by sliding friction

A phase point specifies the coordinate and momentum of a system, and its trajectory has arrows in the direction of time. For a one-coordinate system the phase portrait is a collection of curves in a two-dimensional plane. Unless specified otherwise use axes \((x,p)\), with \(p=m\dot x\), and neglect air resistance. For a pendulum use \((\alpha,\dot\alpha)\), where \(\alpha\) is measured from the downward vertical.
A1. Reflections between walls
Draw the phase trajectory of a free particle reflecting elastically from walls at \(x=\pm L/2\).
A2a. Harmonic phase ellipse
For mass \(m\) under \(F=-kx\), find the phase-trajectory equation and its parameters.
A2b. Harmonic portrait
Draw a harmonic-oscillator phase trajectory and indicate its time direction.
A3. Pendulum phase portrait

A mass \(m\) at the end of a massless rigid rod of length \(L\) swings in gravity \(g\). Draw its phase portrait at arbitrary angle. How many qualitatively different non-equilibrium trajectory types occur, and what conditions distinguish them?
B1. Sliding-friction equation

A block of mass \(m\) on a horizontal surface is attached to a spring of constant \(k\). Static and kinetic friction coefficients both equal \(\mu\). Initially \(x=A_0>0\), velocity zero. Write its equation of motion.
B2. Damped phase portrait and equilibria
Draw the phase trajectory and find equilibrium points.
B3. Stopping interval
Must the block stop at zero extension? Find the width of its possible final-rest region.
B4.drop. Amplitude drop per cycle
Find the drop in successive positive-side turning amplitudes while full cycles continue.
B4.time. Time between maxima
Find the time between successive positive maxima and the sequence \(A(t_n)\).
B5. Motion graph and cycle count
Sketch \(x(t)\), and estimate the number of oscillations before rest.

children.text: Oscillator damped by sliding friction
A1. Reflections between walls

The speed is constant between impacts, giving horizontal segments \(p=\pm p_0\), \(-L/2<x<L/2\). At each wall momentum reverses instantaneously. The top segment runs right and the bottom segment left, with the wall jumps closing a clockwise rectangle.
A2a. Harmonic phase ellipse
Energy conservation gives \(p^2/(2m)+kx^2/2=E\), or \[\frac{x^2}{2E/k}+\frac{p^2}{2mE}=1.\] The semiaxes are \(\sqrt{2E/k}\) in x and \(\sqrt{2mE}\) in p.
A2b. Harmonic portrait
Draw the ellipse centred on the origin. At positive p the coordinate increases, so the trajectory is clockwise. The origin itself is the equilibrium point.
A3. Pendulum phase portrait

Energy is \(E=mL^2\dot\alpha^2/2+mgL(1-\cos\alpha)\). There are three types: closed librations for \(0<E<2mgL\), separatrices for \(E=2mgL\), and continuous rotations for \(E>2mgL\). Plot both rotational directions and both branches of each separatrix. Centres are at \(\alpha=2n\pi\), saddles at \((2n+1)\pi\). The separatrix approaches a top equilibrium only asymptotically. Equilibrium points are excluded from the count.

nodes.alt: Original pendulum energy and phase portrait showing oscillations, separatrices and rotations.

children.text: B1. Sliding-friction equation

While moving, \[m\ddot x=-kx-\mu mg\,\operatorname{sgn}(\dot x).\] At rest it remains stuck if \(|kx|\le\mu mg\). The moving equation alone must not be used to force motion through the sticking region.
B2. Damped phase portrait and equilibria

Define \(c=\mu mg/k\), \(\omega_0=\sqrt{k/m}\). For positive velocity, \((x+c)^2+(p/(m\omega_0))^2\) is constant. For negative velocity replace \(x+c\) by \(x-c\). Join alternating half-ellipses at turning points with clockwise arrows. Their centres are \((-c,0)\) and \((c,0)\), but the actual static equilibria comprise the entire segment \(p=0,|x|\le c\).

nodes.alt: Original clockwise sliding-friction phase trajectory with alternating shifted half-ellipses.

children.text: B3. Stopping interval
It need not stop at zero. Static friction permits any \(-c\le x_f\le c\), whose width is \(2c=2\mu mg/k\).
B4.drop. Amplitude drop per cycle
Each half-cycle reduces turning-distance magnitude by \(2c\). A full cycle therefore gives \(\Delta A=4c=4\mu mg/k\).
B4.time. Time between maxima

Each moving half-cycle lasts \(\pi/\omega_0\). Thus \(t_n=nT\), \(T=2\pi\sqrt{m/k}\), and \(A(t_n)=A_0-4n\mu mg/k\), until sticking interrupts the next half-cycle. The envelope is linear rather than exponential.
B5. Motion graph and cycle count

Draw sinusoidal arcs around alternating shifted centres, under a linearly decreasing envelope, then a horizontal line at the final position in \([-c,c]\). The rough full-cycle estimate is \(N\simeq A_0/(4c)=kA_0/(4\mu mg)\), which is not an exact integer count near the last partial cycle. More precisely, if \(A_0>c\), the number of moving half-cycles is \(\lceil(A_0-c)/(2c)\rceil\). If \(A_0\le c\), the block never starts.
